title: De exterminatione mali et promotione boni

heads.la: TRACTATUS PRIMUS.
heads.en: THE FIRST TREATISE.

heads.la: CAPUT PRIMUM.
heads.en: CHAPTER ONE.

heads.la: CAPUT II. De gemina confessione, et gemina promotione.
heads.en: CHAPTER II. On the twofold confession, and the twofold advancement.

heads.la: CAPUT III. Quomodo confessio criminis valeat ad exterminium mali.
heads.en: CHAPTER III. How the confession of crime avails for the extermination of evil.

heads.la: CAPUT IV. Quomodo confessio laudis valeat ad promotionem boni.
heads.en: CHAPTER IV. How the confession of praise avails for the advancement of good.

heads.la: CAPUT V. Quod prima promotio virtutis sit in contemptu mundi.
heads.en: CHAPTER V. That the first advancement of virtue lies in contempt of the world.

heads.la: CAPUT VI. Quod secunda promotio virtutis sit in contemptu sui.
heads.en: CHAPTER VI. That the second advancement of virtue lies in contempt of self.

heads.la: CAPUT VII. Quomodo per contemptum mundi fiat exterminium mali.
heads.en: CHAPTER VII. How through contempt of the world the extermination of evil comes about.

heads.la: CAPUT VIII. Quod contritio animi nunc sit in adjutorium, nunc ad firmamentum boni.
heads.en: CHAPTER VIII. That contrition of spirit is now for a help, now for the support of good.

heads.la: CAPUT IX. De utili et inutili contritione.
heads.en: CHAPTER IX. On useful and useless contrition.

heads.la: CAPUT X. De gemina cordis compunctione.
heads.en: CHAPTER X. On the twofold compunction of the heart.

heads.la: CAPUT XI. De vano vel vero mundi contemptu
heads.en: CHAPTER XI. On the vain or the true contempt of the world

heads.la: CAPUT XII. Quam sit difficile ad perfectum sui contemptum pertingere.
heads.en: CHAPTER XII. How difficult it is to attain to perfect contempt of self.

heads.la: CAPUT XIII. Quibus modis mens ad plenum sui contemptum eruditur.
heads.en: CHAPTER XIII. By what means the mind is trained to full contempt of self.

heads.la: CAPUT XIV Quod superfluus amor sui inter successus virtutum difficilius vincitur.
heads.en: CHAPTER XIV That superfluous love of self is more hardly overcome amid the successes of the virtues.

heads.la: CAPUT XV. Quomodo gradatim animus ad sui contemptum est promovendus.
heads.en: CHAPTER XV. How the spirit is to be advanced step by step to contempt of self.

heads.la: CAPUT XVI. Quomodo vano amore exhausto animus in Dei amore dilatatur.
heads.en: CHAPTER XVI. How, when vain love has been drained away, the spirit is enlarged in the love of God.

heads.la: CAPUT XVII. De vani amoris defectu, et veri amoris profectu.
heads.en: CHAPTER XVII. On the failing of vain love, and the progress of true love.

heads.la: CAPUT XVIII. Quomodo per vani amoris defectum mentis perturbationes deficiunt.
heads.en: CHAPTER XVIII. How, through the failing of vain love, the perturbations of the mind fail.

heads.la: CAPUT XIX. Cum qua cautela debeamus cordis perturbationes delere.
heads.en: CHAPTER XIX. With what caution we ought to blot out the perturbations of the heart.

heads.la: TRACTATUS SECUNDUS. Ab hoc loco agitur de studio contemplationis, et quomodo vel quantum valeat ad reformationem veri amoris.
heads.en: THE SECOND TREATISE. From this place onward the zeal of contemplation is treated, and how, or how much, it avails for the reforming of true love.

heads.la: CAPUT PRIMUM.
heads.en: CHAPTER ONE.

heads.la: CAPUT II. Qomodo investigatio et retractatio salubrium valeat ad corrigendum animum.
heads.en: CHAPTER II. How the investigation and review of wholesome things avails to correct the spirit.

heads.la: CAPUT III. Quod facilius est animum corrigere quam ejus intima penetrare.
heads.en: CHAPTER III. That it is easier to correct the spirit than to penetrate its inmost parts.

heads.la: CAPUT IV. Quantum valeat cum profunda admiratione infirmitatis nostrae considerationi diutius inhaerere.
heads.en: CHAPTER IV. How much it avails to cleave the longer, with deep wonder, to the consideration of our own infirmity.

heads.la: CAPUT V. Quomodo post plenam correctionem sui, animus ad aeternorum contemplationem introducitur.
heads.en: CHAPTER V. How, after the full correction of self, the spirit is brought in to the contemplation of eternal things.

heads.la: CAPUT VI. Quod in futura vita post aeternorum contemplationem, animus ad omne desiderii sui beneplacitum relaxatur.
heads.en: CHAPTER VI. That in the life to come, after the contemplation of eternal things, the spirit is loosed to every good pleasure of its own desire.

heads.la: CAPUT VII. Quomodo quidam in hac etiam vita ad aeternorum contemplationem sublevantur.
heads.en: CHAPTER VII. How some, even in this life, are lifted up to the contemplation of eternal things.

heads.la: CAPUT VIII. Quod semper oportet per contemplationis studium praevidere quo debeamus per desiderium tendere.
heads.en: CHAPTER VIII. That we ought always, through the zeal of contemplation, to foresee whither we should tend by desire.

heads.la: CAPUT IX. De gemina imperfectione quas semper oportet prae oculis habere.
heads.en: CHAPTER IX. On the twofold imperfection, which we ought always to have before our eyes.

heads.la: CAPUT X. Exemplum vel forma propositae considerationis.
heads.en: CHAPTER X. An example or form of the consideration proposed.

heads.la: CAPUT XI. De his quae pertinent ad meditationem vel contemplationem, et quantum valeant ad virtutis promotionem talium captus.
heads.en: CHAPTER XI. On those things which belong to meditation or to contemplation, and how much the grasp of such things avails for the advancement of virtue.

heads.la: CAPUT XII. De gemina praemeditatione, praemiorum videlicet et meritorum.
heads.en: CHAPTER XII. On the twofold premeditation, namely of rewards and of merits.

heads.la: CAPUT XIII. Quomodo speculationi praemiorum oportet vehementius insistere.
heads.en: CHAPTER XIII. How one must press more vehemently upon the speculation of rewards.

heads.la: CAPUT XIV. Quod speculatio meritorum in duobus constat.
heads.en: CHAPTER XIV. That the speculation of merits consists in two things.

heads.la: CAPUT XV. Quid sit meditationis, et quid sit contemplationis.
heads.en: CHAPTER XV. What belongs to meditation, and what to contemplation.

heads.la: TRACTATUS TERTIUS. Hucusque de boni promotione, abhinc de ejusdem confirmatione.
heads.en: THIRD TREATISE. Thus far concerning the advancement of good; henceforth concerning the confirmation of the same.

heads.la: CAPUT PRIMUM.
heads.en: CHAPTER ONE.

heads.la: CAPUT II. De confirmatione mentis in bono et obduratione mentis in malo.
heads.en: CHAPTER II. On the confirmation of the mind in good and the hardening of the mind in evil.

heads.la: CAPUT III. De malo praesumptionis seu desperationis.
heads.en: CHAPTER III. On the evil of presumption or of despair.

heads.la: CAPUT IV. Quomodo ex malorum nostrorum recordatione oporteat praesumptionem reprimere.
heads.en: CHAPTER IV. How presumption must be repressed out of the recollection of our evils.

heads.la: CAPUT V. Quomodo ex bonorum nostrorum recordatione oporteat desperationem repellere.
heads.en: CHAPTER V. How despair must be driven back out of the recollection of our goods.

heads.la: CAPUT VI. De duodceim principalibus virtutibus in quibus solidandus est animus.
heads.en: CHAPTER VI. On the [sic: duodceim] principal virtues in which the mind must be made solid.

heads.la: CAPUT VII. De soliditate timoris.
heads.en: CHAPTER VII. On the solidity of fear.

heads.la: CAPUT VIII. De gravitate compunctionis.
heads.en: CHAPTER VIII. On the weight of compunction.

heads.la: CAPUT IX. De spei longanimitate.
heads.en: CHAPTER IX. On the longsuffering of hope.

heads.la: CAPUT X. De charitatis integritate.
heads.en: CHAPTER X. On the integrity of charity.

heads.la: CAPUT XI. De maturitate jucunditatis.
heads.en: CHAPTER XI. On the maturity of gladness.

heads.la: CAPUT XII. De asperitate severitatis.
heads.en: CHAPTER XII. On the harshness of severity.

heads.la: CAPUT XIII. De austeritate abstinentiae.
heads.en: CHAPTER XIII. On the austerity of abstinence.

heads.la: CAPUT XIV. De robore patientiae.
heads.en: CHAPTER XIV. On the strength of patience.

heads.la: CAPUT XV. De sollicitudine circumspectionis.
heads.en: CHAPTER XV. On the solicitude of circumspection.

heads.la: CAPUT XVI. De assiduitate speculationis.
heads.en: CHAPTER XVI. On the assiduity of speculation.

heads.la: CAPUT XVII. De certitudine discretionis.
heads.en: CHAPTER XVII. On the certainty of discretion.

heads.la: CAPUT XVIII. De quiete contemplationis.
heads.en: CHAPTER XVIII. On the quiet of contemplation.
